what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 4: Count explanation trees better than the union bound: the 4/27 ceiling. Blocks 25, 30 (PRs #8168, #8174): the ordering proof bounds P(a site is wrong) by a sum over marked explanation trees, P <= eps_1 R(t + eps_2/t^c, eps_1/t^3) with the tree recursion D = (1+xU)^2 (1+3xD)(1+yF)^6, U = (1+xU)^3 (1+yF)^6, F = (1+xU)^3 (1+3xD)(1+yF)^5, R = (1+xU)^3 (1+3xD)(1+yF)^6, whose domain ends at x = 4/27. That ceiling gives p >= 368 at best on (p,1,2), while the executed threshold is p in (10.5, 11). TASK: a provably smaller count. Candidates: (i) many trees explain the same error set: count error SETS (or minimal trees under a canonical order) instead of trees and show the generating function's radius grows; (ii) a two-scale argument: group levels in blocks and iterate the one-block estimate (a renormalization in the style of the multi-scale proofs of stability for cellular automata), giving a threshold independent of 4/27; (iii) inclusion-exclusion to second order with an exact bound on the overlap term. Deliver an exact certificate (rational super-solution) for any new recursion and the threshold it proves; verify the domination of the true error probability on small cones by exhaustive enumeration. DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/beyond-the-union-bound/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/beyond-the-union-bound/<name>/check.py"
